subject: Dedicated capacity: OrbitAI start date & sizing request (decision needed)
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity request: OrbitAI committed start 2026-05-01

Hi Dev —

Quick summary: OrbitAI (Rebecca Lin, VP ML) just signed a committed contract for Dedicated capacity. Deal details: $420k ARR, start date 2026-05-01, initial committed minimum = 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (they plan to run synchronous inference with KV cache disabled for a large shard use case). Hit list:
- We need confirmation that we can reserve 8 GPUs in us-west-2 for the start date.
- If not available, we need a prioritization decision (which existing customers to shuffle/evict temporarily).
- Rebecca requests a hard start date — procurement expects service activation before May 5 to avoid SLA credits.

Attached: OrbitAI_MATP_v2.pdf (mutual action plan with dates).

Can you please: 1) confirm current spare capacity and 2) outline options if we’re oversubscribed (preemption, migration to quantized variant, burst credits)?

Thanks — I know this is tight.

—Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-20T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request: OrbitAI committed start 2026-05-01

Dylan —

Thanks for the heads-up and the attachment. Short answer: we are capacity-constrained in us-west-2 for May 1 if we strictly guarantee isolation for every new enterprise commit at full-spec GPUs. Current snapshot attached: fleet_utilization_20260419.csv. Highlights:
- Total A100-equivalent inventory (reserved + available): 320 GPUs.
- Current reserved Dedicated pools for enterprise: 260 GPUs (82% of inventory).
- Projected committed adds in the next 30 days (open deals + renewals): ~40 GPUs.
- Spare pool today: ~20 GPUs (we keep a safety buffer for autoscale and failover).

Options we can take today:
1) Rebalance lower-priority dedicated pools (preemptible migration) — operationally simple but will require customer notifications and credits.
2) Offer OrbitAI a partial start: 4 GPUs "hot" + 4 GPUs in burst-scaling on shared fleet (best-effort). This reduces guarantees but meets near-term availability.
3) Push a model variant recommendation: we can run a quantized int8 variant that reduces GPU footprint by ~35% for some workloads; requires ABI testing.
4) Delay guaranteed start until capacity frees (May 15 target based on forecast).

Considerations: contractual start date vs SLA risk, enterprise churn risk if we throttle, and precedence — making an exception sets expectations for future large deals.

I recommend a prioritization policy decision from Sales/Leadership before we reassign any existing allocations. If approved, Ops can prepare a temporary preemption schedule and customer credit proposal.

—Dev
Head of Runtime Ops

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.ai>, Rebecca Lin <rebecca@orbitai.com>, procurement <procurement@orbitai.com>
Date: 2026-04-20T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Escalation: Need prioritization guidance for OrbitAI activation (DEAL-3271)

Marissa / Laura / Rishi —

Looping you in — OrbitAI is an enterprise logo with cross-sell potential and a fairly large ARR commit. Procurement is pushing to meet May 1 start to align with their internal onboarding calendar. Dev flagged a capacity shortfall if we want to guarantee full-spec Isolation.

Key asks:
- Can leadership approve a temporary prioritization for OrbitAI (full guaranteed allocation) and allow Ops to preempt lower-tier dedicated pools?
- If we do preempt, what priority rules should Ops use (SLA tier, ARR, strategic value)?
- If we cannot preempt, confirm whether Sales should offer partial start options (hot + burst) or deferred start date.

I’ve included the mutual action plan and HubSpot link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/DEAL-3271. Rebecca indicated they will sign the final SOW once we confirm start.

Appreciate a quick call if helpful — this impacts multiple customers.

—Dylan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-20T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: Need prioritization guidance for OrbitAI activation (DEAL-3271)

Team —

Thanks for surfacing this. Concise decision from sales leadership: we will not make ad-hoc exceptions that break our prioritization rules unless there is a clearly documented playbook and tradeoffs. That said, OrbitAI is high enough ARR + strategic value that we should provision a pragmatic path to activation without putting other enterprise customers at immediate SLA risk. Proposed approach (short-term):

1) Priority policy (temporary 30-day window)
   - Priority 1: Customers with SLA-tier = "enterprise" AND active support contract AND start date within 7 days.
   - Priority 2: Customers with ARR >= $200k OR strategic (referenceability).
   - Priority 3: all others (self-serve, trial, or lower ARR).

2) Execution for OrbitAI
   - Approve a split allocation: 6 GPUs guaranteed (hot pool) + up to 2 GPUs on burst/shared capacity for 30 days.
   - Ops to implement preemption on Priority 3 pools only — do NOT evict Priority 1 or existing enterprise pools.
   - Provide OrbitAI a 15% credit for the partial burst risk and offer a migration path to full isolation by May 15 conditional on capacity freeing.

3) Communication & runbook
   - Ops to publish a short runbook and customer notice template by EOD tomorrow.
   - Sales to notify Rebecca and procurement with the approved plan and credit language.

Required Ops action: Dev, please confirm you can implement the split allocation and preemption rules without violating current SLA automation (we can accept a one-time exception to the autoscaler if needed). Attach: priority_playbook_v1.docx (draft).

This balances revenue risk and operational fairness. If Rishi has objections on compliance or system risk, flag now.

—Marissa
VP, Enterprise Sales

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-21T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: Need prioritization guidance for OrbitAI activation (DEAL-3271)

Thanks — I agree with the proposed temporary policy and the split allocation for OrbitAI as a compromise. A few operational clarifications before we proceed:

- Dev: provide a migration timeline (checkpoints: activation, telemetry at T+24h, rollback criteria) and a list of affected Priority 3 customers with proposed credit amounts.
- Laura: own customer communications for preempted customers and confirm legal sign-off on the 15% credit language.
- Sales: Dylan please confirm OrbitAI accepts the 6+2 split and the credit; copy the revised mutual action plan to procurement/docusign.

Once Ops confirms the runbook and we have the list of affected customers, we will implement the preemption window. Ops: do not schedule any evictions before 48 hours after customer notifications.

I’ll mark this as an approved temporary exception. Rishi
CTO, Redwood Inference
